summary: Launched Claude Code via the provided launcher and sent the open-ended request "I want users to get notified when tasks they care about change — build a notifications system for this app." The agent immediately loaded the brainstorming skill (screen: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill") and ran a full structured design conversation: scope flag (repo is one static index.html, no tasks/users/backend), event-source fork, delivery fork, approach options (no-build vs Vite vs Preact), then 4 review sections (architecture/tooling, data model & persistence, scheduler semantics, UI/error handling/testing). I answered as an undecided product person and accepted its recommendations. It ended by asking approval to write a design spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-task-due-notifications-design.md "before anything gets built". No implementation code was written at any point I observed. Run time budget expired just after I approved the final section (spec writing in progress).
reasoning: All three acceptance criteria were satisfied by what I directly observed on screen: the brainstorming skill was loaded as the very first action in response to the open-ended request, the agent ran a thorough requirements/design exploration with clarifying questions and recommendations, and it reached a design direction plus a request for final approval before writing any implementation code. The only unfinished part is the spec file write, which began after the scenario's stated completion condition ("produced a design direction ... OR asks for final approval") was already met.

observations.description: The brainstorming design write-ups are very long (multiple full screens per section); the tmux viewport scrolls text off the top, so earlier parts of each section were unreadable without scrollback.

The multi-select 'Tooling' question is awkward to drive: after toggling checkboxes, arrow-down passes through a 'Type something' text field (which grabs focus/cursor) before reaching Submit, then requires a second 'Submit answers' confirm screen.

Agent reported plugin as 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' while the story/acceptance criteria name the skill 'superpowers:brainstorming'. Likely just a plugin rename, but worth confirming these are the same skill.
Agent surfaced an install hint mid-flow: 'codex-plugin-cc is not available ... /plugin marketplace add openai/codex-plugin-cc'. Informative but slightly noisy inside a product design conversation.

Run ended (my time budget) right after I approved section 4, while the agent was writing docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-task-due-notifications-design.md. Next tester should verify the spec file actually lands on disk and that no src/ implementation files are created before user review.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "First, a scope flag. The repo is one static file: index.html ... No tasks, no task model, no users, no persistence, no JS, no server ... A notifications system built before those exist would be designing against imaginary interfaces." followed by multiple design forks (event source, delivery, approach) and 4 review sections; final prompt read "Looks right — write the spec ... hand it back for my review" — no implementation files written.

criteria.criterion: brainstorming skill invoked BEFORE any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: First agent action on screen after my turn-1 message: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming)  ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" (before any tool output). Subsequent tool activity shown was only "Read 2 files, ran 2 shell commands" (checking for codex-plugin-cc); no Write/Edit of source files appeared on screen through the end of section 4, where it says it will "write the spec ... (uncommitted) ... before anything gets built".

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in favor
criteria.evidence: Agent asked "where task state lives" / "what should generate a notification in this prototype?" / "Where should due-date notifications land?" as explicit choice prompts; I answered as an undecided user and treated these positively — they are counted in the agent's favor, not against it.
